hints: First check the laser wavelength column: visible light is about $400 \text{ nm}$ to $700 \text{ nm}$, so decide which rows use visible light.
Recall fringe spacing $x = \lambda D/a$, so large slit-screen distance $D$ and small slit separation $a$ give wider, more visible fringes.

Calculate $x$ in $\text{m}$ for the visible-wavelength rows using $\lambda$ in $\text{m}$, $D$ in $\text{m}$ and $a$ in $\text{m}$, then ask which $x$ is millimetres to centimetres rather than micrometres.
walkthrough: Notice the two requirements: the light itself must be visible, and the fringe spacing $x$ on the white screen must be large enough for the eye to resolve, about millimetres or more.
Visible wavelengths are roughly $400 \text{ nm}$ to $700 \text{ nm}$, so $200 \text{ nm}$ is ultraviolet and cannot give visible fringes, which rules out two combinations.
For two-slit interference use $x = \lambda D/a$, where $\lambda$ is wavelength, $D$ is slit-screen distance and $a$ is slit separation.

For the $600 \text{ nm}$, $0.10 \text{ mm}$, $5.0 \text{ m}$ combination: $\lambda = 600 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$, $D = 5.0 \text{ m}$, $a = 0.10 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$, so $x = (600 \times 10^{-9} \times 5.0)/(0.10 \times 10^{-3}) = 0.030 \text{ m}$.
A spacing of $30 \text{ mm}$ is easily seen, whereas the $100 \text{ mm}$ separation gives only $x \approx 6 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$, which the eye cannot resolve. This is option C.

options.A: The $200 \text{ nm}$ wavelength is ultraviolet, not visible light, so no visible fringes can form even though the fringe spacing would be large.
options.B: The $200 \text{ nm}$ wavelength is not visible and the $100 \text{ mm}$ slit separation gives $x \approx 2 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$, far too small to resolve by eye.
options.C: The $600 \text{ nm}$ wavelength is visible red light and $x = \lambda D/a \approx 0.030 \text{ m}$, which is widely spaced enough to see on the screen.
options.D: Although $600 \text{ nm}$ is visible, the $100 \text{ mm}$ slit separation gives $x \approx 6 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$, far too small to see as separate fringes.
